facts.value: 1794 mission to Alaska. Later granted autocephaly by the Russian church

citations.locator: Orthodox Church in America, member profile
citations.excerpt: The Orthodox Church in America traces its roots to the arrival in Alaska in 1794 of missionaries from the monastery of Valamo in Karelia (in the Russian empire).
The Russian Orthodox Church granted complete self-government to the metropolia whereby it became an autocephalous, or fully independent, local Orthodox church.

facts.value_before_verify: 1794 mission to Alaska. Autocephaly granted by the Russian church in 1970

citations.excerpt: The struggle over the identity and the status of the American metropolia was resolved in 1970.
